rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: One view model, three views over it (A Signal Bridge, B Attention Ledger, C Decision Desk), a detail inspector and a text export, in two data modes: `fixture` (the package's synthetic fixtures) and `live` (`worker-list` only).

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: the view is picked once at start-up from the runtime state of the question source. If the question source has not succeeded in this process, the observer starts on A with the gap notice, even in a release whose gate passed. The view never switches automatically mid-session.

rendering_rules.label: UNVERIFIED (beyond copied values)
rendering_rules.text: the design-package prototype is a visual reference only; no production import. Its 116-column collapse claim does not match the built prototype, so width rules come from the Round 2 consensus (A's width matrix, B's x/width coordinates, C's 44-row height contract). The sources name these three artifacts but do not define their contents; only the values copied below are specified, the rest is UNVERIFIED and an open question (`SPEC.md`).

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Header line 1:** `ORCA OBSERVER  mode=fixture|live  scope=<result.scope.source or "scope unknown">  as of <local time of last good poll>`. Fixture mode always reads `SYNTHETIC FIXTURE <variant>, not Orca data`.

rendering_rules.label: CONTRADICTION
rendering_rules.text: The B view adds `read k of N Runs since start; oldest among Runs read` until every Run in the rotation set has been read once. CONTRADICTION: the source's adapter scope-honesty rule (`adapter-contract.md`), T45 and the risks table put this token in every header; which applies is an open question (`SPEC.md`).

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Header line 2, freshness strip (from A):** one cell per source: `worker-list OK 4s` / `STALE 52s` / `FAILED (exit 2) 1m` / `NOT POLLED`. A second cell `messages UNVERIFIED (not read)` stays until QUESTION-OBSERVATION passes. The strip is collection freshness; evidence freshness (`evidence.lastObservedAt`) is shown per row as a plain age, never merged into the source cell.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **COUNTS strip (source-reported), every width of 80 or more:** numbers and denominators only, no bars, no health name. Tokens: `collected n / reported T`, `PARTIAL` when it applies, the scope, `source counts: active a / reclaimable r / retained t / released l` (from `result.counts`, never summed with page-derived counts), `SETTLED unavailable (no source)`, `FROZEN unavailable (no source)`, `cost unavailable`. `collected n / reported T`, `PARTIAL` and scope are never truncated. At narrow widths the strip wraps to a second line before anything is cut; `>` applies only to lower-priority tokens (source age, the `unavailable (no source)` tokens). It is a minimum row and is never dropped.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Footer:** the key list plus `shown x/y | collected n / reported T`.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: rows with historical `terminalState` (released, retained) are hidden by default with a visible `k historical hidden (h)`; `h` shows them; the toggle never changes source counts; historical evidence explicitly linked to a shown item is never hidden. They are never deleted from the snapshot.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Selection** is anchored to identity, never a row index. Worker rows: source namespace + `dispatchId`. Questions (after QUESTION-OBSERVATION): a verified source-scoped question identity, never a worker `dispatchId`. A reordering refresh keeps the cursor on the same identity; if it disappears the cursor stays on `selected <id> no longer in source window` until the user moves, never jumping to another worker.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Truncation:** list cells truncate by display-cell width with a visible `>`. Non-UTF-8 terminals use `--ascii`, which replaces box drawing with `+-|`.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Detail inspector (Enter):** every field untruncated, wrapped by cells: `dispatchId`, `taskId`, `runId`, `resource.worktreeId`, `resource.ownerDispatchId`, `resource.originDispatchId`, `projection.host.id`, `projection.workspace.id`, and `projection.stage.{worker,dispatch,activity,detail}` (sanitized, labelled `worker-reported`; the only place `stage` renders). Absent reads `unknown (absent in source)`.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **`projection.nextAction.kind` is verbatim.** Absent or blank reads `unknown`. Never classified, executed, ranked as an action list or called a question. May be used as a labelled local filter.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: Above the ledger, at every width, the gap notice: `Human questions: source UNVERIFIED, 0 rows interpreted, not "no questions"`. Exact strings by place: this gap notice above the ledger (every view); B's live question-panel block `Question rows: source UNVERIFIED. 0 rows interpreted. This is not "no questions".`; anywhere else the question area reads the shared core `source UNVERIFIED, 0 rows interpreted, not "no questions"`.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: The first observation in a process is the baseline; a restart discloses that a new baseline was taken. `m` records an observer-local mark in memory for this process only. Every row added, removed or changed in `stage` (which `projection.stage.*` subfield is an open question), `nextAction.kind` or `liveness.verdict` since the mark shows `*` and counts in `changed since HH:MM (k)`. Rows on pages not read this cycle read `not reobserved`, not "unchanged". Marking never changes the open count.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Four states per fact:** `known`, `unknown` (source omitted it), `unavailable` (no verified source exists), `stale` (not read successfully within 3 intervals). An aggregate with unknown members is `n+? (k unknown)`. Unknown is never zero or false.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Absent field:** literal `unknown`, muted (plain under NO_COLOR); never `0`, `false`, `-` or blank.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: Unknown is never rendered as 0, false, `-` or blank. Source loss never closes a question, lowers an open count or turns a value into `failed`.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Separate facts:** `workerState`, `dispatchStatus`, `terminalState`, `projection.outcome` are separate raw values. Report status, acceptance, tests and human approval read `unavailable (no source)`. `terminalState=released` is never "done". Help text: "a completed Task can still own a live terminal".

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Stale:** STALE after 3 intervals (45 s at 15 s) with no successful poll, on a local monotonic clock; wall-clock time only prints `HH:MM`. The cell reads `STALE <age>`; values keep their last reading with `as of HH:MM:SS`. Source loss never closes a question, changes the open count or turns a value into `failed`. A failed poll shows `FAILED (<exit code or timeout>) <age>` with sanitized stderr in the inspector.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Collection vs evidence freshness:** source STALE depends on poll success only; a worker's evidence age is a plain age, with no per-row STALE until Orca's timestamp cadence is measured.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Partial pages:** if `page.hasMore` is still true at the call cap: `PARTIAL: collected n of reported T (newest first; oldest rows not read; long-running active workers may be among them)`. Derived counts state denominators, e.g. `nextAction present: 17 of 300 collected (reported 412)`. T comes from the last page read: `reported T (page k)`. `page.total` changing mid-traversal: `reported T1-T2 (changed during read)`. Finished traversal with n not T: `collected n / reported T (mismatch)`. `workers=[]` with T above 0 ends as `PARTIAL (empty page k)`.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Filtered vs global:** a filter always shows `filter <expr>: k of n collected` beside the unfiltered `source counts: ...`; source counts are a different scope (terminal accounting) and never summed into "workers".

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Overflow:** `x/y shown`; `+N more` counts only rows not shown, never the selected visible row.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **100-row cap:** (a) `worker-list` returns at most 100 rows per page and the observer follows `nextCursor` up to the call cap. (b) If `check --all` is admitted at QUESTION-OBSERVATION, the question panel title reads `at most 100 rows per read, not 100 questions; older history not available`; a retained question that leaves the window stays open with `no longer in source window (last seen HH:MM)`.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Question area:** before QUESTION-OBSERVATION `source UNVERIFIED, 0 rows interpreted, not "no questions"`, no number; no count is ever derived from `result.count`. After the gate: `collected n unique / reported T`, `changed during read` and mismatch notes, rotation with a per-scope `revisit ~Ns` token, and an empty rotation set reads `message source not read: no eligible scope; coverage unknown`.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Seen is not resolved:** the big count is observed open questions, or `unknown (no question source)`. `m` moves an item from `not marked` to `marked looked`; the count stays. `closed by evidence` reads `unavailable` until a closure source exists. No key, timer or source loss lowers the open count; only explicit closure evidence, not available in the MVP. No verified source records explicit closure today, so every retained question renders `open, closure source unavailable`; it is never shown as resolved and never quietly dropped.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Empty states (T33):** with no message source the question area carries the gap-notice wording above, never `no questions` (the source's T9 and empty-state rule also use `0 rows interpreted (contract UNVERIFIED)`; this spec uses the source's Change 28 question-area wording everywhere for one consistent string); `worker-list returned 0 workers in scope=bound` names the scope; fixture `empty` renders `no observed items in this source window; not proof none exist`.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **Cost and tokens:** `cost unavailable`, never `$0`; no progress bar from tokens or activity.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: **SETTLED and POLICY FROZEN (T34):** live both read `unavailable (no source)`; in fixture mode a frozen item keeps a `FROZEN` marker no other state overrides.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: Untrusted source text cannot corrupt the terminal, and the view stays legible at 160, 116 and 80 columns, under NO_COLOR and in ASCII. ... Injection fixtures render literally; CJK/emoji truncate on cell width; geometry and too-narrow/too-small diagnostics match; nothing blinks

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: T29: `injection` (CSI, OSC 8 hyperlink, unterminated OSC, 8-bit C1 `\x9b`, BEL, bidi Cf such as U+202E, terminal title set) leaves no ESC, C1 or Cf byte in render or export. T30: CJK/emoji identifiers truncate by cells; no overflow, no split double-width char.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: Worker text containing Rich markup (e.g. `[bold]`) renders literally.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: T26: `NO_COLOR=1` and `NO_COLOR=yes` emit no SGR colour; meaning stays readable as words.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: T28: SGR 5/6 (blink) never appears.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: | Mouse, themes, blinking, animation | Out of scope; no blinking is a constraint. |

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: Deterministic, bounded collection: no LLM in the loop, fixed 15 s cycle, at most 5 subprocesses per cycle and 8 MiB output per call.

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: | `r` refresh key | Would add a second polling path; `m` takes its place. |

rendering_rules.label: SPEC
rendering_rules.text: T40 | Fake monotonic clock: STALE at 45 s without success, unaffected by wall-clock jumps; backoff caps at 60 s; overrunning call killed and strip shows `cycle overran (Ns)`.

rendering_rules.label: NOT SPECIFIED
rendering_rules.text: No colour palette or glyph-to-meaning table is defined. Only: `unknown` is muted (plain under NO_COLOR) [rendering-rules.md:51]; `*` marks changed rows [rendering-rules.md:46]; `>` marks truncation [rendering-rules.md:24]; `+-|` replaces box drawing under `--ascii` [rendering-rules.md:24]; meaning stays readable as words under NO_COLOR [acceptance-tests.md:19]; themes out of scope [rendering-rules.md:81].

widths.text: At 116 columns or more B draws the full frame with `right = width - 43`. From 80 to 115 it uses the single-column narrow layout. Under 80 every view shows `terminal too narrow (min 80)` above the COUNTS strip, and the strip's denominators still print.
Left `OPEN HUMAN QUESTIONS` (x=1, width 114). ... Right top `SEEN IS NOT RESOLVED` (x=117, width 42)
**116 columns.** Same structure with `right = 73`; question panel 70 wide; right column stays 42; ledger in its 116-column line form.

**80 columns.** Single column: header, freshness strip, COUNTS strip, `SEEN IS NOT RESOLVED n`, question lines (fixture) or the UNVERIFIED notice (live), then the ledger in its 80-column form. The invariant lines stay: "Questions stay until explicit resolution." and "No reply observed is not delivery failure." RETAIN CONTEXT is reachable only through the inspector.

One row per worker from `worker-list`, in source order: `dispatchId`, run (labelled "run", never "orchestrator"), `workerState`, `dispatchStatus`, `terminalState`, `projection.outcome` (raw), `projection.nextAction.kind`, `liveness.verdict (liveness.source)`, evidence age. There is no `stage` column at any width; `stage` is in the inspector.
widths.note: 160 not stated explicitly for this row form; it is the full form, with 116 and 80 forms given separately

widths.text: At 116 columns: `<kind> <dispatchId> <liveness.verdict> <age>`, with `stage` moved into the inspector. At 80 columns: `kind`, a dispatch ID cell-truncated with `>`, and an age.
T23: at 160/116/80 every screen line has `cell_len <= W`.

bindings.text: **Keys (inspection and local filtering only):** Up/Down or `j`/`k` move, `Enter` opens detail, `Esc` returns, `/` local text filter, `h` show/hide historical rows, `m` mark a look, `e` write an export, `q` quit. No `r` key: refresh runs on the fixed 15 s cycle. No key maps to an Orca call.

focus.text: No per-panel scrolling, no multi-pane focus.

selection_anchor.text: A reordering refresh keeps the cursor on the same identity; if it disappears the cursor stays on `selected <id> no longer in source window` until the user moves, never jumping to another worker.

help.label: NOT SPECIFIED
help.text: No help key is bound. Only help text content is named: Help text: "a completed Task can still own a live terminal". Footer carries the key list.

no_key_to_orca.text: T3: no key maps to an Orca call.

out_of_scope_input.text: Fleet SIGNALS bars, an `r` refresh key, persisted "last look" across runs, mouse, themes, animation, blinking, and Windows interactive keyboard input.
| Windows keyboard input | The stdlib reader is POSIX-only; on Windows `--once` prints a text export. |

key_reader_spike_gate.text: Spike: Rich Live with the raw stdlib key reader; on failure switch to Textual, never both. Render timing and per-call timeouts measured.
Every fixture variant renders at all three widths with the label "synthetic fixture, not live evidence"; the key-reader spike result is recorded (T50, T6, T16).

**Spike first (R0):** Rich Live with the raw key reader. If the spike fails, switch to Textual. Never build both. Textual is not first because of its maintenance risk and UNVERIFIED plain-text export.
| Hand-written key reader misbehaves | Terminal left in raw mode | Restore in `finally` and on SIGINT/SIGTERM; `--once` needs no raw mode; R0 spike decides, Textual fallback |

switch_to_textual_rule.text: Stack is Python + Rich as a `superclaude observe`-style subcommand in the IronClaude repo; the key-reader spike comes first; Textual replaces Rich only if the spike fails, never both (`stack.md`).

The B screen below is the post-QUESTION-OBSERVATION view, and its degraded form is used for the owner's R0 comparison.

acceptance_tests_ux.line: no key maps to an Orca call.
a fake always returning `hasMore=true` stops at the 5-call cap and renders `PARTIAL: collected 500 of reported T`.
a fake sleeping past the measured per-call timeout shows `FAILED (timeout)`; the cycle ends within the 15 s budget.
same input renders byte-identical text twice.
`base` (8 orchestrators, 80 sessions) in fixture mode lists every question oldest first with requester/owner and affected IDs.
after `m`, a fixture step changing one `nextAction.kind` stars exactly that row and shows `changed since HH:MM (1)`.
live mode with no message source shows `Human questions: source UNVERIFIED, 0 rows interpreted, not "no questions"` (`rendering-rules.md`) and titles the ledger `worker-reported, not questions`.
`m` on every item leaves the open count unchanged.
`source-loss` keeps the open count and every retained item; nothing becomes resolved or failed.
an item missing next cycle stays, marked `no longer in source window`.
`missing-fields` renders `unknown` for every absent field; `0`/`false` never stand in (asserted per field).
`terminalState=released` with `outcome` absent never renders `done`, `complete` or `settled`.
report, acceptance, tests and approval each render `unavailable (no source)` live.
matrix {5, 8, 10 orchestrators} x {50, 80, 100 sessions} x {160, 116, 80 columns} (27 renders); every count line matches `k of n`, every hidden overflow shows `x/y shown` with y = fixture total.
`page.total=287` with 100 rows shows `collected 100 / reported 287`, never `287 workers`; `page.total` absent shows `reported unknown`.
(R2 placeholder, skipped until QUESTION-OBSERVATION): question panel title contains `at most 100 rows per read, not 100 questions` and `bounded best effort; coverage unknown`.
`shared-unmapped` shows two sessions sharing one `worktreeId` as two rows each naming it, and a session with no worktree as `worktree unknown`; no count divides one by the other.
released/retained rows hidden by default with `k historical hidden (h)`; after `h` listed with `terminalState`, not counted active.

`duplicate-out-of-order` shows `k duplicate rows ignored`; an older `observedAt` never overwrites a newer one; a row missing both timestamps is flagged `order unknown`; a backward timestamp shows `conflict (time went back)`.
at 160/116/80 every screen line has `cell_len <= W`.
`long-identifiers` truncates with `>` in lists; inspector shows the full ID.
reorder between cycles keeps selection on the same row ID.
`NO_COLOR=1` and `NO_COLOR=yes` emit no SGR colour; meaning stays readable as words.
`e`/`--once` writes the record export: no ESC byte, full IDs, no truncation.
SGR 5/6 (blink) never appears.
`injection` (CSI, OSC 8 hyperlink, unterminated OSC, 8-bit C1 `\x9b`, BEL, bidi Cf such as U+202E, terminal title set) leaves no ESC, C1 or Cf byte in render or export.
CJK/emoji identifiers truncate by cells; no overflow, no split double-width char.
cost renders `cost unavailable`, never `$0`; no progress from tokens or activity.

Removing `result`, `result.workers` or `result.page.hasMore` gives `FAILED (shape)` with last good snapshot kept; removing `result.scope` shows `scope unknown`; removing `page.total` shows `reported unknown`; removing an inner `projection.*` field gives `unknown`, not an error.
`empty` renders `no observed items in this source window; not proof none exist`, never `no questions`.
Fixture mode renders `FROZEN`; live mode renders SETTLED and POLICY FROZEN as `unavailable (no source)`, never blank or zero.
COUNTS strip appears at 80, 116 and 160; priority tokens never truncated; below 80 reads `terminal too narrow (min 80)`.
Aggregate with k unknown members renders `n+? (k unknown)`, never a clean `n`.
Same `dispatchId` from different source namespaces stays two rows.
STALE at 45 s without success, unaffected by wall-clock jumps; backoff caps at 60 s; overrunning call killed and strip shows `cycle overran (Ns)`.
First observation is the baseline with no change flags; a row dropping out shows `not reobserved`.
Successful poll with old worker evidence shows poll age and evidence age separately and does not mark the source STALE.
With the selected row visible and others hidden, `+N more` excludes the selected row.
Worker text containing Rich markup (e.g. `[bold]`) renders literally.
Default view chosen at start-up, never switches mid-session; header shows `read k of N Runs since start` (which views carry it is an open question, `SPEC.md`).
At 1,001 retained questions, eviction does not lower the open total; count reads `unknown (retention exceeded)` with the retained count; oldest first.

Before QUESTION-OBSERVATION the question area reads `source UNVERIFIED, 0 rows interpreted, not "no questions"`; no count from `result.count`; `changed during read`, mismatch, `revisit ~Ns` and empty-rotation-set notes render per `rendering-rules.md`.
Screen renderer and record export read the same view model; an ID truncated with `>` on screen appears in full in the export.
When height cannot hold coverage, scope and PARTIAL ahead of optional panels, a too-small diagnostic shows.
R0 renders of A, B, C at 160/116/80 each carry "synthetic fixture, not live evidence" with a degraded version beside each.
one run in a real terminal confirms cell truncation of a CJK identifier as T30 asserts headlessly; reported as a manual check, not a test pass.
Render with `Console(width=W, record=True, color_system=None or "standard")` and read `export_text()`. ... No TTY, no live Orca.

signal_bridge_layout.explanation: Neither candidate layout is named. The spec never mentions PLAN.md, an owner-row cockpit, an intervention rail, a change ribbon, a session register or signal counts (grep across the folder found none). It defines R1 as a composition: A's worker ledger plus the COUNTS strip, the freshness strip and B's gap notice. Fleet SIGNALS bars are explicitly left out.

evidence.text: Recorded owner decision 1: R1 = A's worker ledger + COUNTS strip + B's one-line question-source gap notice; B after QUESTION-OBSERVATION with A's ledger one key away; C only behind QUESTION-LINK.
**Recorded owner decision 1 (staged releases, binding):** R1 = Signal Bridge's worker ledger on the verified `worker-list`, carrying Attention Ledger's "question source UNVERIFIED" notice.
| Fleet SIGNALS bars | No verified mapping from `workerState`/`outcome` to "settled"; the COUNTS strip is shown instead. |

**A is stronger on day-one live data:** every A panel except the request panel fills from `worker-list` today, and A answers "is the fleet alive?" at a glance. Weakness: a single request slot (`_request` in `signal_bridge`) repeats the recency bias #409 complains about; its 116- and 80-column builds drop SIGNALS; the prototype does not match the brief's collapse claim (X-001).
The sources name these three artifacts but do not define their contents; only the values copied below are specified, the rest is UNVERIFIED and an open question (`SPEC.md`).
